comment: Known-dead routes between the declared capability registry (workers/nitro-worker/src/capabilities.js), the measured host route table (workers/nitro-enclave-host/src/routes.rs) and the web proxies (apps/web/app/api/**/route.*). This is a RECORD OF DEBT, not an allowance, and it only shrinks. scripts/check-capability-route-parity.mjs enforces that in the tree on every run: every dead lane must be listed; an entry that is not actually dead fails; every entry needs a reason, an owner and an expires that is a real date, later than today and at most 60 days away; and a proxy entry pins the target and method it was recorded with, so re-pointing a proxy at another dead route fails. CI also runs the gate with --base <the pull request's base commit>: an entry that is not in the base file, a later expires, or a re-pointed proxy fails. Deleting an entry is the only edit that passes both, and it is what CU-149 did when it added the five read-only catalog routes to the host, repaired the GET/POST mismatch on /api/runtime/keys/derived and removed the two proxies aimed at lanes the host will not serve. An entry may never be added to admit a newly declared lane: that is the failure the gate exists to catch. Same 'absence without a dated record is a hard failure' rule as deploy/nitro/kms/attestation-pins.json.
recorded_against: neo-os-services main 9c3019c (the three route sources are byte-identical on main 0c45a78)
closes_with: CU-149 (host catalog routes and dead web proxies): the five catalog routes landed on the host and the five dead web proxies are resolved (2026-10-13). They ship dark under DEC-CU-30 until the enclave rebuild (OP-11); the ids still listed below are the debt this row deliberately did not close.

The lane stays off the host on purpose: transaction submission goes through the relayer, not the enclave. Retiring the registry id is a capability-surface decision, not this row's.
